deviations.what: keep t3's candidacy decoupling and ADD receiving-side work: a box must not shed a pooled arrival on a host-level pressure verdict alone. Also accept t3's two renegotiated pool-pressure tests (test_busy_peer_that_is_itself_busy_is_not_forwarded_to, test_both_boxes_busy_sheds_locally_and_never_forwards) as deliberate contract changes under h6.
deviations.reason: implementing c5 revealed the fix is one-sided: the receiver still sheds a marked arrival under its own pressure (test_a_marked_arrival_under_local_pressure_gets_the_local_429 still passes) and a peer 4xx is relayed never retried, so a forward to a pressure-busy peer returns the same 429 after a wasted round trip. The deployed Spark scenario - false iowait, idle GPU - would still refuse forwarded work, so success signals c15/c17/c18 are unreachable by candidacy decoupling alone. The /challenge pass swept seven lenses but none followed the request end-to-end to ask whether a newly-selectable peer would actually serve it.

deviations.what: t10 (live acceptance) must run AFTER the final PR is opened, not before it as the plan's wave order implies. Sequence becomes: merge wave 4 -> open PR (gate 3) -> CI publishes 0.67.0.devN to TestPyPI -> rebuild both gateways against it -> run t10 -> append the evidence transcript to the same PR.
deviations.reason: the gateway is not run from source: Dockerfile.gateway installs lobes-cli==${MODEL_GEAR_VERSION} from PyPI or a TestPyPI dev index, and the deployed Thor gateway is running 0.63.0.dev428 fetched that way. Per CLAUDE.md only a PR publishes a .devN to TestPyPI, so the artifact t10 needs to deploy does not exist until the PR is open. The plan placed t10 in wave 5 ahead of gate 3 without accounting for how code reaches a box.

deviations.what: correct and extend the d1 record: (a) there were THREE test renegotiations, not two -- the third is tests/test_gateway_selection.py::test_affinity_preferred_busy_falls_back_to_availability -> ..._full_..., plus two unrecorded fixture rewrites (test_no_selectable_candidates_returns_none, test_higher_weight_peer_beats_lower_weight_local); (b) d1 misattributes test_both_boxes_busy_sheds_locally_and_never_forwards to test_gateway_pool_pressure.py -- it lived in test_proxy_integration.py; (c) honesty condition h2 was NOT met as written and is hereby amended: 'existing selection tests pass unchanged for any fixed weight' is false at exactly weight=1.0, which c22/h15 deliberately reinterpreted from a measured one-slot capacity into the uncalibrated sentinel.
deviations.reason: task t7, the guard task, exists to enforce h6's 'explicit, recorded renegotiation' standard and found the record incomplete. Leaving three renegotiations unrecorded would defeat the very condition the guard was written to check. The h2 amendment is the substantive item: select_replica is genuinely not the same function of its arguments as before at weight=1.0, and that change is correct under c22 but contradicts h2's wording.

deviations.what: add work not in the confirmed plan (tracked here as t12, a task the plan never had): wire the ten <PREFIX>_MAX_ACTIVE knobs and GATEWAY_CAPACITY_KILL_SWITCH into the gateway service's compose passthrough, plus a guard test deriving the required env set from _config.py itself. The guard also caught three PRE-EXISTING inert knobs unrelated to this work: GATEWAY_FORCE_STRICT_TOOLS (documented to operators in env.example, never plumbed) and FALLBACK_URL / FALLBACK_SERVED_NAME.
deviations.reason: the feature was INERT in every real deployment. lobes/templates/fleet/docker-compose.yml enumerates each env var the gateway receives (there is no env_file), and none of the capacity knobs were listed -- so an operator .env value could never reach the container. Every test passed because tests construct config in-process, bypassing compose entirely, making this class of gap structurally invisible to the suite. t10 would have measured no effect and we would have wrongly concluded capacity routing does not help. Found by the docs agent, which could not honestly write that compose covers these knobs.

deviations.what: engine saturation must drive SELECTION only, not SHEDDING: remove the engine signal from the shed decision in _pressure_policy.py while keeping active>=capacity in _selection._is_selectable, so a saturated fleet falls through to local queueing (the pre-pool behaviour) instead of refusing the request 429. (Amends the receiving-side work recorded in d1.)
deviations.reason: t10 measured it live on the Spark+Thor pair: an 8-way flood through the pool served 4 and shed 4 with HTTP 429 (aggregate 62.27 tok/s over the survivors), where the same flood bypassing the pool served 8/8 with zero errors (42.77 tok/s). Forwarding itself works -- 2 requests carried X-Lobes-Proxied-By: spark with reasons local-busy-forwarded and peer-less-loaded, proving the d1 two-sided decoupling against a Spark still flagged busy at 68 percent iowait -- but d1's receiving-side work made active>=capacity a shed signal, which routes a saturated request to the busy path (429) instead of _PoolFallthrough's local dial. Capacity was specified as a routing preference, not admission control; converting a burst that used to queue into refusals is an availability regression no claim in the frame asks for.
